claim: p97/Cdc48 ATPase and its ubiquitin receptors Ufd1-Npl4 are essential to unfold ubiquitylated proteins in many areas of eukaryotic cell biology.
source: The p97/Cdc48 ATPase and its ubiquitin receptors Ufd1-Npl4 are essential to unfold ubiquitylated proteins in many areas of eukaryotic cell biology.
evidence: This is a general statement about the essential role of p97/Cdc48 and Ufd1-Npl4, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: In yeast, Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 is controlled by a quality control mechanism whereby substrates must be conjugated to at least five ubiquitins.
source: In yeast, Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 is controlled by a quality control mechanism, whereby substrates must be conjugated to at least five ubiquitins.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work and is presented as established knowledge about yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.

claim: Mammalian p97-UFD1-NPL4 is governed by a complex interplay between additional p97 cofactors and the number of conjugated ubiquitins.
source: Here, we show that mammalian p97-UFD1-NPL4 is governed by a complex interplay between additional p97 cofactors and the number of conjugated ubiquitins.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Human p97-UFD1-NPL4 has a high ubiquitin threshold for substrate unfolding.
source: Using reconstituted assays for the disassembly of ubiquitylated CMG (Cdc45-MCM-GINS) helicase by human p97-UFD1-NPL4, we show that the unfoldase has a high ubiquitin threshold for substrate unfolding, which can be reduced by the UBX proteins UBXN7, FAF1, or FAF2.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from reconstituted assays shown in the manuscript.

claim: The UBX proteins UBXN7, FAF1, or FAF2 can reduce the ubiquitin threshold of human p97-UFD1-NPL4.
source: Using reconstituted assays for the disassembly of ubiquitylated CMG (Cdc45-MCM-GINS) helicase by human p97-UFD1-NPL4, we show that the unfoldase has a high ubiquitin threshold for substrate unfolding, which can be reduced by the UBX proteins UBXN7, FAF1, or FAF2.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from reconstituted assays.

claim: UBX proteins function by binding to p97-UFD1-NPL4 and stabilising productive interactions between UFD1-NPL4 and K48-linked chains of at least five ubiquitins.
source: Our data indicate that the UBX proteins function by binding to p97-UFD1-NPL4 and stabilising productive interactions between UFD1-NPL4 and K48-linked chains of at least five ubiquitins.
evidence: This is an interpretation of experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Stimulation by UBXN7 is dependent upon known ubiquitin-binding motifs.
source: Stimulation by UBXN7 is dependent upon known ubiquitin-binding motifs, whereas FAF1 and FAF2 use a previously uncharacterised coiled-coil domain to reduce the ubiquitin threshold of p97-UFD1-NPL4.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from truncation analysis of UBXN7 shown in Figure 5.

claim: FAF1 and FAF2 use a previously uncharacterised coiled-coil domain to reduce the ubiquitin threshold of p97-UFD1-NPL4.
source: Stimulation by UBXN7 is dependent upon known ubiquitin-binding motifs, whereas FAF1 and FAF2 use a previously uncharacterised coiled-coil domain to reduce the ubiquitin threshold of p97-UFD1-NPL4.
evidence: This is a novel finding supported by experimental data from truncation analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Deleting the Ubxn7 and Faf1 genes impairs CMG disassembly during S-phase and mitosis.
source: We show that deleting the Ubnx7 and Faf1 genes impairs CMG disassembly during S-phase and mitosis and sensitises cells to reduced ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from mouse ES cells shown in Figure 6.

claim: Deleting the Ubxn7 and Faf1 genes sensitises cells to reduced ubiquitin ligase activity.
source: We show that deleting the Ubnx7 and Faf1 genes impairs CMG disassembly during S-phase and mitosis and sensitises cells to reduced ubiquitin ligase activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing sensitivity to MLN-4924 treatment in Figure 7.

claim: Multiple UBX proteins are important for the efficient unfolding of ubiquitylated proteins by p97-UFD1-NPL4 in mammalian cells.
source: These findings indicate that multiple UBX proteins are important for the efficient unfolding of ubiquitylated proteins by p97-UFD1-NPL4 in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: AAA+ ATPases comprise hexameric rings with a central pore in which loops from each subunit form a 'spiral staircase' around the unfolded polypeptide chain.
source: These comprise hexameric rings with a central pore, in which loops from each subunit form a 'spiral staircase' around the unfolded polypeptide chain.
evidence: This is established knowledge about AAA+ ATPase structure, supported by citations (Puchades et al., 2020; Seraphim and Houry, 2020; Zhang and Mao, 2020).

claim: ATP hydrolysis drives conformational changes within the ATPase hexamer, leading to translocation of the unfolded polypeptide along a 'conveyor belt' of pore loops.
source: ATP hydrolysis drives conformational changes within the ATPase hexamer, leading to translocation of the unfolded polypeptide along a 'conveyor belt' of pore loops.
evidence: This is established knowledge about AAA+ ATPase mechanism, supported by citations (Puchades et al., 2020; Seraphim and Houry, 2020; Zhang and Mao, 2020).

claim: p97/Cdc48/VCP is a AAA+ ATPase with orthologues in all three domains of life.
source: p97/Cdc48/VCP is a AAA + ATPase with orthologues in all three domains of life (Bodnar and Rapoport, 2017a; van den Boom and Meyer, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Eukaryotic p97/Cdc48/VCP unfolds highly stable proteins to prepare them for subsequent degradation by the proteasome.
source: Eukaryotic p97/Cdc48/VCP unfolds highly stable proteins to prepare them for subsequent degradation by the proteasome (van den Boom and Meyer, 2018; Verma et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: p97/Cdc48/VCP is required for disassembly of the replisome at the end of chromosome replication.
source: For example, p97/Cdc48/VCP is required for disassembly of the replisome at the end of chromosome replication (Dewar et al., 2017; Franz et al., 2011; Maric et al., 2014; Moreno et al., 2014; Sonneville et al., 2017; Villa et al., 2021)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: p97/Cdc48/VCP is required for release of newly synthesised protein phosphatase I from an inhibitory protein complex.
source: release of newly synthesised protein phosphatase I from an inhibitory protein complex (van den Boom et al., 2021; Weith et al., 2018)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: p97/Cdc48/VCP is required for release of DNA repair complexes from chromosomes.
source: release of DNA repair complexes from chromosomes (Kilgas et al., 2021; Meerang et al., 2011; van den Boom et al., 2016)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: p97/Cdc48/VCP is required for the proteasomal degradation of misfolded membrane proteins.
source: and the proteasomal degradation of misfolded membrane proteins (Ravanelli et al., 2020; Wolf and Stolz, 2012; Wu and Rapoport, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Dominant mutations in human p97 are associated with a late-onset multisystem proteinopathy.
source: Consistent with the important roles of p97/Cdc48/VCP in eukaryotic cell biology, dominant mutations in human p97 are associated with a late-onset multisystem proteinopathy (Johnson et al., 2010; Meyer and Weihl, 2014; Watts et al., 2004)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: p97 is upregulated in certain cancer types.
source: whilst p97 is upregulated in certain cancer types (Li et al., 2021; Tsujimoto et al., 2004)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: p97 is a target for anti-cancer therapies.
source: and is a target for anti-cancer therapies (Anderson et al., 2015; Deshaies, 2014; Magnaghi et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: p97/Cdc48/VCP associates with a wide range of adaptor proteins, many of which are still understood poorly.
source: p97/Cdc48/VCP associates with a wide range of adaptor proteins, many of which are still understood poorly (Buchberger et al., 2015; Hänzelmann and Schindelin, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Some p97/Cdc48/VCP adaptor proteins recognise substrates directly.
source: Some recognise substrates directly (van den Boom et al., 2021; Weith et al., 2018)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Some p97/Cdc48/VCP adaptor proteins contain ubiquitin-binding motifs that link p97/Cdc48/VCP to poly-ubiquitylated substrates.
source: but others contain ubiquitin-binding motifs that link p97/Cdc48/VCP to poly-ubiquitylated substrates (Bandau et al., 2012; Buchberger et al., 2015; Stach and Freemont, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Ufd1 and Npl4 form a heterodimeric receptor for polyubiquitin chains that include linkages via lysine 48 (K48) of ubiquitin.
source: The best characterised ubiquitin adaptors of p97/Cdc48/VCP are Ufd1 and Npl4, which form a heterodimeric receptor for polyubiquitin chains that include linkages via lysine 48 (K48) of ubiquitin (Bodnar and Rapoport, 2017a; Pan et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The Ufd1–Npl4 complex helps to recruit Cdc48 to polyubiquitylated substrates.
source: Studies of yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 have shown that the Ufd1–Npl4 complex not only helps to recruit Cdc48 to polyubiquitylated substrates but is directly involved in the first step of protein unfolding
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations (Bodnar and Rapoport, 2017a; Ji et al., 2022; Twomey et al., 2019).

claim: The Ufd1–Npl4 complex is directly involved in the first step of protein unfolding, which initiates within the ubiquitin chain rather than the substrate itself and is independent of ATP hydrolysis by Cdc48.
source: Studies of yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 have shown that the Ufd1–Npl4 complex not only helps to recruit Cdc48 to polyubiquitylated substrates but is directly involved in the first step of protein unfolding, which initiates within the ubiquitin chain rather than the substrate itself and is independent of ATP hydrolysis by Cdc48 (Bodnar and Rapoport, 2017a; Ji et al., 2022; Twomey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Ufd1-Npl4 underpin a potentially universal mechanism for the recognition and unfolding of Cdc48 substrates that are conjugated to K48-linked ubiquitin chains, without any requirement for direct recognition of the folded substrate protein itself.
source: In this way, Ufd1-Npl4 underpin a potentially universal mechanism for the recognition and unfolding of those Cdc48 substrates that are conjugated to K48-linked ubiquitin chains, without any requirement for direct recognition of the folded substrate protein itself (Ji et al., 2022; Twomey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an interpretation of previous work supported by citations.

claim: This mechanism exploits the reduced structural stability of ubiquitin within polyubiquitin chains.
source: It is likely that this mechanism exploits the reduced structural stability of ubiquitin within polyubiquitin chains (Carrion-Vazquez et al., 2003; Morimoto et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculation based on previous work, supported by citations.

claim: The yeast Ufd1–Npl4 complex uses multiple ubiquitin-binding sites to interact with up to five ubiquitins within a K48-linked chain.
source: Structural studies suggested that the yeast Ufd1–Npl4 complex uses multiple ubiquitin-binding sites (Park et al., 2005; Sato et al., 2019) to interact with up to five ubiquitins within a K48-linked chain (Twomey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 can only process substrates with at least five conjugated ubiquitins.
source: Such assays showed that yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 can only process substrates with at least five conjugated ubiquitins (Deegan et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous work, supported by citation.

claim: The 'five-ubiquitin threshold' represents a quality control mechanism that protects substrates from premature unfolding, by coupling Cdc48 activity to efficient ubiquitylation.
source: This 'five-ubiquitin threshold' represents a quality control mechanism that protects substrates from premature unfolding, by coupling Cdc48 activity to efficient ubiquitylation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of previous work, supported by citation (Deegan et al., 2020).

claim: Until now, the ubiquitin threshold for substrate unfolding by mammalian p97-UFD1-NPL4 had not been determined.
source: Until now, the ubiquitin threshold for substrate unfolding by mammalian p97-UFD1-NPL4 had not been determined.
evidence: This statement establishes the novelty of the current study's findings.

claim: Ufd1-Npl4 are essential for yeast Cdc48 and metazoan p97/VCP to unfold ubiquitylated substrates.
source: Although Ufd1-Npl4 are essential for yeast Cdc48 and metazoan p97/VCP to unfold ubiquitylated substrates (Blythe et al., 2017; Bodnar and Rapoport, 2017b; Deegan et al., 2020; Mukherjee and Labib, 2019)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Eukaryotic cells including yeast and metazoa encode a range of other adaptor proteins, which combine ubiquitin-binding motifs with a UBX domain that associates with the amino terminus of p97/Cdc48/VCP.
source: eukaryotic cells including yeast and metazoa also encode a range of other adaptor proteins, which combine ubiquitin-binding motifs with a UBX domain that associates with the amino terminus of p97/Cdc48/VCP (Alexandru et al., 2008; Hänzelmann and Schindelin, 2017; Kloppsteck et al., 2012; van den Boom and Meyer, 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: UBXN7/UBXD7, FAF1, FAF2/UBXD8, and UBXN1/SAKS1 all co-purified from human cells with UFD1-NPL4 in addition to p97.
source: Strikingly, studies of such ubiquitin-binding adaptors of human p97 found that UBXN7/UBXD7, FAF1, FAF2/UBXD8, and UBXN1/SAKS1 all co-purified from human cells with UFD1-NPL4 in addition to p97 (Alexandru et al., 2008; Hänzelmann et al., 2011; Lee et al., 2013; Raman et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: FAF1 and UBXN7 associate preferentially with p97-UFD1-NPL4 compared to p97 alone.
source: Moreover, in vitro studies of purified FAF1 and UBXN7 showed that both factors associate preferentially with p97-UFD1-NPL4 compared to p97 alone (Hänzelmann et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citation.

claim: The mechanism or regulation of p97-UFD1-NPL4 have additional layers of complexity that remain to be explored.
source: These findings suggested that the mechanism or regulation of p97-UFD1-NPL4 have additional layers of complexity that remain to be explored.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from previous findings, setting up the rationale for the current study.

claim: The segregase activity of mammalian p97-UFD1-NPL4 is controlled by a combination of ubiquitin chain length and multiple UBX proteins.
source: Here, we show that the segregase activity of mammalian p97-UFD1-NPL4 is controlled by a combination of ubiquitin chain length and multiple UBX proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Reconstituted human p97-UFD1-NPL4 only unfolds substrates that are conjugated to extremely long ubiquitin chains.
source: In contrast to yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4, reconstituted human p97-UFD1-NPL4 only unfolds substrates that are conjugated to extremely long ubiquitin chains.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Association of p97-UFD1-NPL4 with the UBX proteins UBXN7, FAF1, or FAF2 reduces the ubiquitin threshold to a comparable level to yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4, dependent upon conjugating five ubiquitins to the substrate.
source: However, association of p97-UFD1-NPL4 with the UBX proteins UBXN7, FAF1, or FAF2 reduces the ubiquitin threshold to a comparable level to yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4, dependent upon conjugating five ubiquitins to the substrate.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: UBX proteins ensure that p97-UFD1-NPL4 can unfold ubiquitylated proteins with high efficiency in mammalian cells.
source: In this way, such UBX proteins ensure that p97-UFD1-NPL4 can unfold ubiquitylated proteins with high efficiency in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Human p97-UFD1-NPL4 disassembles CMG complexes with very highly ubiquitylated CMG-Mcm7.
source: In contrast, although p97-UFD1-NPL4 rapidly disassembled CMG complexes with very highly ubiquitylated CMG-Mcm7 (Figure 2B, lanes 17–18 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, lanes 7–9)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Human p97-UFD1-NPL4 is almost inactive against CMG complexes with up to ~12 ubiquitins conjugated to CMG-Mcm7.
source: the human enzyme was almost inactive against CMG complexes with up to ~12 ubiquitins conjugated to CMG-Mcm7 (Figure 2B, lanes 15–16 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, lanes 1–3; also see below, Figure 4C, lanes 3–4), even in the presence of a large excess of unfoldase (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The yeast and human unfoldases have important differences in their requirements for processing ubiquitylated substrates.
source: These findings indicated that the yeast and human unfoldases have important differences in their requirements for processing ubiquitylated substrates.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing yeast and human enzymes.

claim: Human UFD1-NPL4 and yeast Ufd1-Npl4 determine the ubiquitin threshold of their cognate unfoldase enzymes.
source: These findings indicated that human UFD1-NPL4 and yeast Ufd1-Npl4 determine the ubiquitin threshold of their cognate unfoldase enzymes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Human UFD1-NPL4 and yeast Ufd1-Npl4 employ a similar mechanism to initiate the unfolding of ubiquitylated substrates by p97/Cdc48.
source: It is likely that human UFD1-NPL4 and yeast Ufd1-Npl4 employ a similar mechanism to initiate the unfolding of ubiquitylated substrates by p97/Cdc48.
evidence: This is speculation based on structural and functional similarities, supported by citations and experimental data.

claim: Human UFD1-NPL4 and yeast Ufd1-Npl4 bind to the amino terminal face of human p97/yeast Cdc48, with Npl4 forming a tower adjacent to the central p97 pore.
source: Both adaptor complexes bind to the amino terminal face of human p97/yeast Cdc48, with Npl4 forming a tower adjacent to the central p97 pore within which unfolded peptides are translocated (Bodnar et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2021a; Pan et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Human UFD1-NPL4 and yeast Ufd1-Npl4 utilise conserved ubiquitin-binding modules to recognise K48-linked ubiquitin chains.
source: Moreover, human UFD1-NPL4 and yeast Ufd1-Npl4 utilise conserved ubiquitin-binding modules to recognise K48-linked ubiquitin chains, via multiple contacts including the top of the NPL4 tower and the UT3 domain of UFD1 (Ji et al., 2022; Pan et al., 2021b; Park et al., 2005; Pye et al., 2007; Sato et al., 2019; Twomey et al., 2019; Ye et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Binding of K48-linked ubiquitin chains to yeast Ufd1-Npl4 leads to unfolding of a ubiquitin moiety, which then interacts with a groove on the surface of the Npl4 tower before entering the central pore of Cdc48.
source: Studies of the yeast unfoldase showed that binding of K48-linked ubiquitin chains to Ufd1-Npl4 led to unfolding of a ubiquitin moiety, which then interacts with a groove on the surface of the Npl4 tower before entering the central pore of Cdc48 (Twomey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citation.

claim: Mutations of conserved residues in the yeast Npl4 groove blocked substrate unfolding by yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: Correspondingly, mutations of conserved residues in the Npl4 groove blocked substrate unfolding by yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4 (Twomey et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citation.

claim: Mutation of conserved residues in human NPL4 (NPL4-AAE) blocked the disassembly of ubiquitylated CMG helicase.
source: We found that mutation of the equivalent residues in human NPL4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A, B, NPL4-AAE) blocked the disassembly of ubiquitylated CMG helicase (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C, compare lanes 3–4 and 7–8)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The NPL4-AAE mutation does not affect the association of NPL4 with UFD1.
source: without affecting the association of NPL4 with UFD1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The NPL4-AAE mutation does not affect the interaction of UFD1-NPL4 with p97.
source: or the interaction of UFD1-NPL4 with p97 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The NPL4-AAE mutation does not affect the interaction of UFD1-NPL4 with folded K48-linked polyubiquitin.
source: or folded K48-linked polyubiquitin (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: Human p97-UFD1-NPL4 initiates substrate unfolding via an unfolded ubiquitin intermediate, analogous to the action of yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
source: These data suggested that human p97-UFD1-NPL4 also initiates substrate unfolding via an unfolded ubiquitin intermediate, analogous to the action of yeast Cdc48-Ufd1-Npl4.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and comparison with yeast system.

claim: Yeast Ufd1-Npl4 and human UFD1-NPL4 are considerably more divergent in primary sequence, compared to yeast Cdc48 and human p97.
source: However, yeast Ufd1-Npl4 and human UFD1-NPL4 are considerably more divergent in primary sequence, compared to yeast Cdc48 and human p97 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, C), suggesting some degree of functional diversification.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Human NPL4 has a ubiquitin-binding Zinc finger (NZF) at the carboxy-terminal end of the protein, which is not present in the yeast orthologue.
source: Moreover, human NPL4 has a ubiquitin-binding Zinc finger ('NPL4-like Zinc Finger' or NZF) at the carboxy-terminal end of the protein, which in vitro represents the highest affinity binding site for ubiquitin in human NPL4 (Meyer et al., 2002; Tsuchiya et al., 2017) and is not present in the yeast orthologue.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Deletion of the NPL4-NZF does not impair association with UFD1 or p97.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Meyer et al., 2002), deletion of the NPL4-NZF did not impair association with UFD1 of p97 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, D)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and previous studies.

claim: Deletion of the NPL4-NZF largely abrogates the interaction of UFD1-NPL4 with K48-linked ubiquitin chains in vitro.
source: but largely abrogated the interaction of UFD1-NPL4 with K48-linked ubiquitin chains in vitro (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The NPL4-NZF was found to be dispensable in human cells for the degradation of misfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (ERAD).
source: Nevertheless, the NPL-NZF was previously found to be dispensable in human cells for the degradation of misfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum (Ye et al., 2003), a process known as ERAD that is dependent upon ubiquitylation and the p97-UFD1-NPL4 unfoldase.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citation.

claim: The evolutionarily conserved low affinity binding sites for K48-linked ubiquitin chains in human UFD1-NPL4 are sufficient to initiate the unfolding of ubiquitylated substrates of p97.
source: This suggested that the evolutionarily conserved low affinity binding sites for K48-linked ubiquitin chains in human UFD1-NPL4, at the top of the NPL4 tower and in the UT3 domain of UFD1 (Ji et al., 2022; Pan et al., 2021b; Park et al., 2005; Pye et al., 2007; Sato et al., 2019; Twomey et al., 2019; Ye et al., 2003), are sufficient to initiate the unfolding of ubiquitylated substrates of p97.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from previous work and experimental data, supported by citations.

claim: Human p97-UFD1-NPL4-∆NZF still supports the disassembly of heavily ubiquitylated CMG helicase in reconstituted in vitro assays, albeit with reduced efficiency compared to wild-type NPL4.
source: Indeed, we found that human p97-UFD1-NPL4-∆NZF still supported the disassembly of heavily ubiquitylated CMG helicase in reconstituted in vitro assays, albeit with reduced efficiency compared to wild-type NPL4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C, compare lanes 1–6).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The dynamic association of the NPL4 tower and UFD1-UT3 domain of human UFD1-NPL4 with very long K48-linked ubiquitin chains is sufficient to initiate substrate unfolding, dependent upon the NPL4 groove.
source: Considered together with the data and previous observations discussed above, these findings indicated that the dynamic association of the NPL4 tower and UFD1-UT3 domain of human UFD1-NPL4 with very long K48-linked ubiquitin chains is sufficient to initiate substrate unfolding, dependent upon the NPL4 groove.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data and previous observations.

claim: Additional ubiquitin binding by the NPL4-NZF domain is not an essential part of the mechanism of substrate unfolding, but likely increases the efficiency of substrate engagement by human p97-UFD1-NPL4.
source: Additional ubiquitin binding by the NPL4-NZF domain is not an essential part of the mechanism of substrate unfolding, but likely increases the efficiency of substrate engagement by human p97-UFD1-NPL4, as does increased length of the K48-linked ubiquitin chains.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: The UBX proteins FAF1, FAF2, UBXN7, and UBXN1 were previously found to co-purify with ubiquitin chains, p97 and UFD1-NPL4 from human cell extracts.
source: In this regard, it is interesting that the UBX proteins FAF1, FAF2, UBXN7, and UBXN1 were previously found to co-purify with ubiquitin chains, p97 and UFD1-NPL4 from human cell extracts (Alexandru et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies, supported by citation.

claim: FAF1, FAF2, UBXN7, and UBXN1 all bind directly to p97-UFD1-NPL4 in vitro.
source: Moreover, we found that all four factors bound directly to p97-UFD1-NPL4 in vitro (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; the association of each UBX protein with UFD1-NPL4 was dependent upon the presence of p97).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The association of each UBX protein with UFD1-NPL4 is dependent upon the presence of p97.
source: Moreover, we found that all four factors bound directly to p97-UFD1-NPL4 in vitro (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; the association of each UBX protein with UFD1-NPL4 was dependent upon the presence of p97).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The interaction of UBXN1 with p97-UFD1-NPL4 is relatively weak, both in vitro with recombinant proteins and in human cells.
source: Nevertheless, the interaction of UBXN1 with p97-UFD1-NPL4 was relatively weak, both in vitro with recombinant proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and in human cells (Alexandru et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and previous studies.

claim: UBXN1 does not significantly alter the in vitro activity of the p97-UFD1-NPL4 unfoldase.
source: UBXN1 did not significantly alter the in vitro activity of the p97-UFD1-NPL4 unfoldase (Figure 4C), consistent with the weak interaction of UBXN1 with p97-UFD1-NPL4.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: FAF1, FAF2, and UBXN7 all stimulate the disassembly of ubiquitylated CMG by human p97.
source: In contrast, FAF1, FAF2, and UBXN7 all stimulated the disassembly of ubiquitylated CMG by human p97 (Figure 4D, lanes 1–2, 5–6, and 9–10).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: CMG disassembly by FAF1, FAF2, and UBXN7 is still dependent upon the presence of UFD1-NPL4.
source: In each case, disassembly was still dependent upon the presence of UFD1-NPL4 (Figure 4D, lanes 3–4, 7–8, and 11–12).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: FAF1, FAF2, and UBXN7 stimulate the unfoldase activity of p97-UFD1-NPL4 when the K48-linked ubiquitin chains attached to substrate are of limiting length.
source: These data indicated that FAF1, FAF2, and UBXN7 stimulate the unfoldase activity of p97-UFD1-NPL4 when the K48-linked ubiquitin chains attached to substrate are of limiting length.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: Helicase disassembly by human p97-UFD1-NPL4 in the presence of FAF1, FAF2, or UBXN7 requires five or more ubiquitins on the CMG-Mcm7 subunit.
